**Runtime Default Font**:

The VitaDeck-provided sans-serif font (DejaVu Sans) used for text when a **Deck App** does not request a **Deck App Font** or explicitly requests the reserved default font name. lines.text: > **Domain expert:** "No — load declared **Deck App Fonts** when the **Deck App Package** starts so rendering does not partially proceed with font errors."
> **Dev:** "Must each Deck App declare every pixel size it will use?"
> **Domain expert:** "No — a loaded **Deck App Font** renders at the requested **Font Size**; size-specific font atlases are a future rendering-quality optimization."

lines.text: - "font size" could mean CSS points, scaling, or theme tokens; resolved: **Font Size** is a raw pixel value in the **VitaDeck Runtime API**.
- "default font" could mean Raylib's built-in bitmap font or a bundled VitaDeck typeface; resolved: use a VitaDeck-provided sans-serif **Runtime Default Font**.
- "`default` font" could mean an app-declared font name or VitaDeck fallback; resolved: `default` is VitaDeck-reserved and selects the **Runtime Default Font**.
- "font fallback" could hide invalid packages; resolved: missing or unsupported declared **Deck App Fonts** fail package validation instead of silently falling back.

- "font fallback" could hide invalid packages; resolved: missing or unsupported declared **Deck App Fonts** fail package validation instead of silently falling back, while a valid **Deck App Font** falls back to the **Runtime Default Font** per character it lacks.
- "font loading" could mean lazy render-time loading or package startup loading; resolved: declared **Deck App Fonts** load when the **Deck App Package** starts.
- "font sizes" could imply package-declared preloaded size sets; resolved: **Deck App Fonts** render at arbitrary raw-pixel **Font Size** values for now.
- "providing fonts" could mean hand-editing the package output; resolved: authors declare **Deck App Fonts** in SDK configuration and the **VitaDeck SDK** copies them into the package.
- `version` (optional): semver written to the package manifest. Defaults to `version` in `package.json`.

- `fonts` / `images` (optional): name → file path, relative to the project and inside it. Names start with a letter and use letters, digits, `_` or `-` (max 63 characters); `default` is reserved for fonts. Up to 32 of each. Fonts: `.ttf`, `.otf`, `.fnt`, `.bdf`. Images: `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.bmp`, `.tga`, `.gif`, `.psd`, `.hdr`, `.pic`, `.qoi`. The build copies them into the package and fails if a file is missing.
Reference assets by name, never by path: `<Text font="title" …>`, `<Image image="logo" …>`.
Reference assets by name, never by path: `<Text font="title" …>`, `<Button font="title" fontSize={24} …>`, `<Image image="logo" …>`.

Text, Button and TextInput take any `fontSize` in pixels, and text is UTF-8. Without `font` they use the runtime's DejaVu Sans. Characters a `.ttf` or `.otf` font lacks render in DejaVu Sans; a character neither has renders as a box. `.fnt` and `.bdf` fonts have no fallback.
### TypeScript
<TextInput x={20} y={80} width={400} height={56} value={name} onChange={setName} placeholder="Your name" />;

`maxLength` (default 256, at most 2048) counts like `string.length`. It takes focus like a `Button`, with `focusColor` as its outline (default: `textColor`). Text is UTF-8; characters outside the runtime font render as boxes.
`maxLength` (default 256, at most 2048) counts like `string.length`. It takes focus like a `Button`, with `focusColor` as its outline (default: `textColor`).
